title: Transactional Cost Map & Pricing Scenarios UI prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a high-fidelity prototype and interaction spec for a Transactional Cost Map: a token-level, per-request trace that lets product and finance teams explore how individual requests accumulate cost across model variants, routing tiers, prefixes (cached vs cold), and pricing scenarios. The view should support on-demand exports (CSV/NDJSON), scenario simulation toggles (batching, quantization, routing to cheaper variants), and concise pricing pattern recommendations. Deliverables: Figma prototype, export schema, acceptance criteria, and a short handoff doc for frontend engineers.
acceptance_criteria: Figma prototype covering list, detail, and scenario panels
Export schema documented and example CSV/NDJSON produced
Interactive pricing scenario toggles in prototype (batch size, quantization, route override)
Design tokens and spacing follow console design system
Accessibility checklist passed for primary flows (keyboard nav, color contrast)
comments: 2025-03-04 Maya Chen: Kickoff — scoped MVP as three panes: Request list (filterable), Transaction detail (trace per token and cost attribution), Scenario panel (price simulator + export). Linked initial discovery notes and sample logs.

2025-03-06 Aidan Brooks: Early wireframes uploaded to Figma. Preferred a compact row layout for list to allow dense viewing for high-volume customers. Flagged potential performance constraints for large exports.

2025-03-07 Riley Patel (PM): Reviewed flows — asked for clearer indication of cached vs cold cost and a sticky breakdown summary when scrolling the trace. Raised question about default export granularity (per-token vs per-request).

2025-03-09 Maya Chen: Updated prototype with a compact timeline visualization (mini-sparkline per request) and a hover interaction that surfaces prefix cache hits and KV cache size estimate. Added prototype toggles for simulated quantization delta and autoscaling burst credit usage.

2025-03-10 Design critique notes by Design Team: 1) Rename 'Transaction' to 'Request Trace' to reduce mental model confusion. 2) Move pricing scenario controls to a collapsible right rail to avoid disrupting the trace detail flow. 3) Add an inline help tooltip explaining 'effective unit price' vs 'list price'.

2025-03-11 Engineering feasibility review (ENG-91207): Backend can stream request traces but will need a new compact export endpoint to avoid returning full model weights. Suggested CSV rows: request_id, timestamp, model_variant, token_index, token_text, token_cost_usd, cache_state, latency_ms, route_tier.
2025-03-12 Aidan Brooks: Prototype handed off to FE with notes. Created a small PR template for the export endpoint and linked GH-1248 for backend work. Ready for PM sign-off for release planning.
decisions: Show per-token cost as primary granularity in trace detail with an orthogonal per-request summary row
Default export granularity: per-request with optional per-token toggle to limit payload size
Pricing scenario controls live in a collapsible right rail and should persist across list/detail navigation
Include simulated 'effective unit price' derived from selected scenario (batching + quantization + route) in the top summary bar
Export formats: CSV for spreadsheets, NDJSON for analytics pipelines
next_steps: PM sign-off on export schema and default granularity (due 2025-03-14)
Eng (backend) to implement compact export endpoint and simulated pricing API (linked ENG-91207)
Frontend to import Figma tokens and build prototype components (FE-PR GH-1248)
Accessibility pass and small perf budget review for large exports
Schedule stakeholder demo with Finance and Customer Success (week of 2025-03-17)
notes: Design rationale: Users asked for a 'trace' metaphor during interviews; this helps correlate token-level actions (cache hit/miss, reroute) to dollar impact.
Risk: Per-token exports can be very large for customers with long context lengths; bounded default and paging recommended.
Opportunities: This view can feed the pricing patterns engine — surfaced recommendations could appear as 'apply recommended pricing profile' in rollout flows.
